review_notes: Read the whole file and the relevant Mathlib adjugate/inverse lemmas (adjugate_mul_distrib, adjugate_one, coe_units_inv). Checked the downstream uses of adjugateGL in the SlashAdjugate and Petersson files. Those uses only rewrite with adjugateGL_eq_scalar_mul_inv, which is correctly not a simp lemma because it would expand adjugateGL into the inverse. adjugateGL_eq_inv and the det-smul-inv lemma are correctly not simp: they have hypotheses, and A⁻¹ unfolds to adjugate, so simp could cycle. The orientation of the simp lemmas that are tagged (val, one, mul) looks fine. The only issue I could support is a minor one: redundant simp arguments that duplicate the @[simp] tag on adjugateGL_val. I did not run Lean, so I did not check that other possibly useful simp lemmas, such as one for adjugateGL g⁻¹, would be confluent. No downstream use needs one.

findings.problem: adjugateGL_val is already tagged @[simp], so passing it explicitly to simp is redundant. The same redundancy appears in adjugateGL_eq_scalar_mul_inv at line 132. This blurs which lemmas the default simp set provides. It also hides the fact that the proofs depend on adjugateGL_val being in the simp set.
findings.proposed_change: Write `simp` in adjugateGL_one. In adjugateGL_eq_scalar_mul_inv, drop `adjugateGL_val` from the simp list and keep only the lemmas that are not simp: `Matrix.adjugate_eq_det_smul_inv ...`, `Matrix.smul_eq_diagonal_mul` and `Matrix.scalar_apply`.
findings.benefit: The proofs show which facts come from the simp set and which are supplied by hand. This makes the simp interface of adjugateGL easier to read and keeps the proofs stable if the simp attribute is later changed.
